1.plain: Two sides sit past the 80° valve and two sit under it, and nothing crossed this morning. Iran 79° (6.9 — unchanged: the rial is flat at 230,800, the 'struck in 7 days' component stays 6 with nothing hit on the Iranian side since Qeshm on Sep 16, and the talks component stays 'signals only' — Qatar says it is 'shuttling' with 'several proposals', Naqvi is due in Tehran today, Pezeshkian flies Tuesday, but there is no live channel; the tanker UKMTO logged as #140 is a hit ON shipping and enters no Iran component; regime 6.0, no Gulf act against Iran) — the 07:00 crossing below the valve is still Sam's call. US 82° (7.3 — unchanged: Brent's fall to $101.4 trimmed the door component and the calendar at 43 days lifted the election component by about as much; Reuters/Ipsos 35% is the approval input, 'fired' 7 on the Sep 14–15 MQ-1s until Sep 22 — still above the valve, no crossing; Washington's only word is Trump's Sunday 'deciding mode'). Saudi–UAE 84° (7.6: 'struck' already 10 on the Taif death; the Italian-jet hit cannot raise it; revenue unresolved — Arab News says exports are back above 4m b/d, a press carry, not a print). Small Gulf 75° (6.6), below the valve for a tenth day — the crossing is still held. If the rial firms, Iran's next mechanical step down is 6.8 at ~228,000; one confirmed US strike on an Iranian asset puts it back to 7.3; Brent back above ~$104 lifts the US pot to 7.4, and a fall to ~$92 would take it to the valve.
1.trade: Brent fell a fourth session to $101.4 by 10:08 UTC on the diplomacy read (Qatar 'shuttling', Trump 'probably' open to Pezeshkian, Xi in Washington Wed–Fri) and did not react to UKMTO #140 — the market is pricing the table, not the water. The US pot at 82° needs Brent above ~$104 to tick up and ~$92 to reach the valve; a confirmed IRGC claim of #140 or a named hull would be the first thing to put the risk premium back.

2.plain: The door is quiet and a hull was hit in it this morning. UKMTO's sixtieth report (#140, issued Sep 21) says a tanker on an INBOUND transit was struck by an unknown projectile, two crew have minor injuries and the ship is continuing to its next port under its own power; Al Jazeera carries it; nobody has claimed it and CENTCOM has said nothing — rung 5 is held for Sam. The counts: Sep 20 closed at 6 in / 14 out with 53 hulls in the strait, the tenth day in a row under ten inbound; the AIS poller counts 13 crossings in the 24 h to 10:00 UTC Sep 21 (4 in, 9 out — two oil/chemical tankers of 84,715 dwt, a 63,672-dwt bulk carrier, a container ship and the small LPG/chemical tanker out; the 46,187-dwt chemical tanker, a general cargo, a cargo vessel and a tug in) with 589,913 bbl of petrochemical exports and no crude, 1,277 ships in the two gulfs; Sep 21 has 31 hulls inside, one in and two out after ten hours. UKMTO's weekly 'single-digit' line and Reuters/Kpler's 12-vessel weekend say the same thing; Cooper's 'six-month high' stands alone. PortWatch still ends Sep 13 at a 7-day average of 5.3 commercial transits — eight days behind. The live layer at 10:00 UTC: 109 aircraft, 1,321 ships, all tiles OK; the three military flags in the Iran box are Qatari PC-21 trainers over Doha, none over Iran; two US-military tails on adsb.lol — a Navy Citation westbound over central Saudi Arabia and a KC-46-class tanker off Oman's Batinah coast.
2.trade: Each week under 10 transits/day has lifted Brent; creditor selling steepens the curve.

3.plain: Carriers hold outside Iran's 300 km ring; the fight is inside it. USNI Sep 14: both carriers and the Boxer group in the Arabian Sea, no US warship named inside the Gulf; Ross back with Bush.
3.trade: A carrier inside the ring is the tell for a wider war.

4.plain: Thirty-nine items wait for Sam's tick — ONE new at Sep 21 03:00: UKMTO Attack #140, an inbound tanker struck by an unknown projectile in the strait with two crew hurt and the ship sailing on (UKMTO + Al Jazeera, two regions), proposed as rung 5 (ship attacked; crew hurt, none killed) with the 'IRGC fires on / seizes tanker' signal — actor ir by the strait's pattern, as every unattributed UKMTO hull since Sep 12 has been proposed; UKMTO names no perpetrator and no IRGC claim has matched it. Alone it would move the posteriors from [0.969, 0.015, 0.008, 0.008] to [0.972, 0.025, 0.002, 0.001], 'force' from 50 to 52 and 'Bigger war' from 33 to 34; approved with the three held tanker rungs (Sep 12, 16, 17) the entries compound in date order. Still not held: the IRGC's 'another MQ-1' (single region at six hours — no CENTCOM word, no US official, not on UKMTO), Mohebbi's 'change the geography of the war', the NPT bill (paper, with the Presiding Board), Qatar's 'several proposals' and Xi's visit (the talks thread already held as 2026-09-20 11:00-1). The two Sep 17 rows left the 72-hour list on schedule; their rungs stay pending. The tanker rungs of Sep 12/16/17 hold on an unchanged UKMTO list; the MQ-1 rung holds at ~85 h of CENTCOM silence; the Riyadh rung still leans to rejection; the Italian-jet rung has no update; the Iran and Small Gulf valve crossings are unchanged.
4.trade: A confirmed pipeline hit is the rung-7 print that re-prices Brent; watch for a rung-9 act (a US warship actually hit) or the first rung-10 act since February.

5.plain: Most likely next 14 days: Iran seizes or fires on a tanker; a Gulf energy strike is the second card; the Oman MOU track is the third — and two held signals (the UAE crown prince's meeting, Bahrain's refusal) would move the deal card up and the widen-the-war card up respectively if ticked.
5.trade: Tanker rates and war-risk premia up; XLE over SPX; long-dated Brent calls cheap if force-scenario odds are right.

6.plain: Iran wants to force an escalation before Nov 3; the US wants to squeeze and hold.
6.trade: No deal premium: fade rallies on 'talks' headlines unless a convoy actually transits.

7.plain: America's quiet bill: gas, yields, rial.
7.trade: DXY firm short-term (safe haven), soft long-term (reserve share).

8.plain: Iran and the small Gulf states pay; Israel doesn't.
8.trade: Qatar and Kuwait sovereign spreads wider; Israeli equities unaffected.

9.plain: Russia and Egypt win; Asia's importers lose; creditors trim.
9.trade: Long RUB oil revenue proxies; short INR/JPY on oil-import stress.

10.plain: The engine (lobby, arms, oil) still beats the brake (voters) — but the gap is closing.
10.trade: LMT/RTX hold while engine ≥8; first brake-over-engine print is the sell signal.

11.plain: Bigger war 33%, Stuck 31%, Strait regime 17%, Signed deal 8%, Regime change 6%.
11.trade: Bigger-war above 30% is the level to hedge with long-dated Brent calls; Signed deal above 20% is the level for Brent < $85.

12.plain: Weak signals: whether UKMTO #140 gets a name, flag, owner or position — and whether the IRGC Navy claims it (the 'Trend' was claimed within the hour; #139 never was); whether CENTCOM or a US official ever confirms the IRGC's 'another MQ-1' (the Sep 14–15 drones took two days to reach CBS); whether Naqvi actually arrives in Tehran today and with what (Baghaei, twice: no US message); whether Qatar's 'several proposals' become a named channel or a Trump–Pezeshkian slot before Wednesday's speech; what Xi's Wednesday–Friday visit does to China's line on the Iran file at the Council; whether Trump's Tuesday UNGA speech is the Iran-bomb speech and whether the six Gulf-leader meetings look like a coalition pitch; whether Ghalibaf lets the NPT-withdrawal bill out of the Presiding Board; whether Mohebbi's 'new weapons' is followed by anything shown; whether PortWatch's Monday publication of Sep 14–20 settles the count now that UKMTO, Reuters/Kpler and the board's AIS agree against NCAGS/Cooper; whether Arab News's 'over 4 million barrels daily' for Saudi exports is matched by a Kpler or Argus print; whether Riyadh ever attributes the airport fuel-depot fire; whether Brent's fourth session down survives the US open and the DGS10/DGS30 prints; what USNI's Monday tracker says about which US hulls are still inside the Gulf.

tiles.counter: one scale for every pot: 100° = boils over (a side gives up its aim); 80° = the emergency valve, past which a side is forced to escalate and acts against its own interest. Underneath, every pot shares one trigger on the 0–10 score — 7.0, the valve (re-fit monthly, the same for all four); the display maps 7.0 to 80° and 10 to 100°, so a degree means the same thing in every pot and the gap from 80° to 100° is a side's remaining tolerance

tiles.counter: Covers official accounts only (central banks, sovereign funds), not hedge funds or UK banks, and only what is custodied at the New York Fed — a central bank moving paper to Euroclear shows as a sale here without selling. It is a market-value level, so yields move it too. No public source gives daily per-country holdings; this is the closest weekly proxy.
tiles.moves: Every Thursday evening: append the new Wednesday level (the 19:00 run); a weekly drop above $30B is the alert line; cross-check with Japan MoF weekly securities flows (Thursday) when available

tiles.counter: AIS shows only ships that broadcast — dark tankers and most warships are invisible; ADS-B shows only aircraft with transponders on — military aircraft over Iran do not broadcast, so an empty sky is 'not seen', not 'not there'. Dead-reckoned positions are extrapolations, not fixes. Thermal anomalies cannot say what burned or who lit it
tiles.source: Live layer: every AIS commercial ship from hormuz.data-tracking.net /api/ships (MarineTraffic feeds, 30-min polls) and every ADS-B aircraft from adsb.lol (four 250-nm circles) — rebuilt every 10 minutes by a GitHub Action (live.json) and, between fixes, moved along last course and speed (dead reckoning, ≤20 min). Basemap: NASA VIIRS true colour via GIBS, newest complete pass (date on the toggle). Fire dots: VIIRS 375 m thermal anomalies, last 48 h (flares are normal; a new dot at a port, refinery or base is the signal). US warship positions: USNI Fleet & Marine Tracker (weekly, Monday) — the tracker names the sea, the point inside it is ours (JUDGMENT); roster as of Sep 8: George Washington + George H.W. Bush CSGs and the Boxer ARG in the Arabian Sea, Lincoln departed for Thailand Sep 2 · Satellite checks (S badges): Sentinel-2 via GIBS, 30 m, latest cloud-free pass per site, vessel counts at pier/anchor are our reading (JUDGMENT)

Scoreboard = latest official prints, not forecasts: Rosstat Q2 GDP (Aug 12), Bank of Russia balance of payments (Jan–May goods surplus, Q2 current account), MinFin monthly oil & gas revenue and H1 deficit; China NBS Q2 GDP / Jul activity / PPI-CPI (Aug 17) and General Administration of Customs August trade (Sep 8); Korea MOTIE August trade (Sep 1), Bank of Korea Q2 advance GDP and GDI, KRX H1 operating profit, SK hynix 2Q26; Brazil IBGE Q2 GDP, MDIC monthly trade, BCB Focus survey; Malaysia DOSM July trade (Aug 20), MITI, IMF WEO Jul 2026 for the growth forecast. Export-engine bars: same customs/ministry releases; Russia surplus = Jan–May monthly average; ringgit at 4.2 RM/$.
tiles.counter: These are correlations with the war window, not attributions: Korea and Malaysia are riding the AI-chip cycle, China's record exports are partly tariff front-running and a weak yuan, Brazil's crude surge started before March. Russia's beat is Q2 y/y against a weak 2025 base and its budget oil take is still falling. Most trade prints are one month; Q2 GDP is preliminary and gets revised.
tiles.moves: Monthly: China customs (~7th), Korea MOTIE (1st), Brazil MDIC (1st week), Malaysia DOSM (~20th), Russian MinFin oil & gas revenue (3rd). Quarterly: Q3 GDP prints late Oct (Korea, China) and Nov (Russia, Brazil). IMF October WEO replaces the July forecast column.
tiles.trade: The trade is not Russia or China — it is the AI-hardware exporters (Korea, Malaysia, Taiwan) and non-Gulf crude exporters (Brazil) that carry a war premium without war exposure; China gets export volume but no domestic lift; Russia gets prices and a current-account cushion but not budget cash.
